notes: Translated line by line; the swap stays with the narrator as in the source, while the two men visibly hand each other their sandwiches. Two men are muzhik and his double muzhik-sosed in flat caps; the barman walks over to them.
title: Eigenes Essen

lines.text: Zwei Männer trinken in einer Kneipe.
Sie packen die Butterbrote aus, die ihre Frauen liebevoll für sie geschmiert haben, und fangen an zu essen.
Sie dürfen hier nicht Ihr eigenes Essen essen.
Also tauschten sie ihre Butterbrote.

notes: Dialogue kept word for word; the opening narration is cut because the picture shows the boy on the park bench with his chocolate bar. 'Fucking' softened to 'freaking' in the clean line.
title: His Own Business

lines.text: Eating that many chocolate bars is bad for you.
My great grandfather lived to be one hundred and five.
And he ate that much chocolate?
No. But he minded his own freaking business.
lines.uncensored: No. But he minded his own fucking business.

notes: Literal translation; the opening narration is cut because the picture shows the boy on the bench with the chocolate bar. The swear goes in as «блядь», softened to «блин».
title: Не в своё дело

lines.text: Есть столько шоколадок вредно.
Мой прадедушка дожил до ста пяти лет.
И он ел столько шоколада?
Нет. Но он, блин, не лез не в своё дело.
lines.uncensored: Нет. Но он, блядь, не лез не в своё дело.

notes: Literal translation; the opening narration is cut because the picture shows the boy on the bench with the chocolate bar. 'Scheiß' softened to 'Mist' in the clean line.
title: Der Urgroßvater

lines.text: So viele Schokoriegel zu essen ist ungesund.
Mein Urgroßvater ist hundertfünf Jahre alt geworden.
Und er hat so viel Schokolade gegessen?
Nein. Aber er hat sich um seinen eigenen Mist gekümmert.
lines.uncensored: Nein. Aber er hat sich um seinen eigenen Scheiß gekümmert.

notes: Source wording kept, title line dropped. Two stops on the same road with a wipe for the next day; the new penguin puppet stands for the ten penguins by the van and wears dark glasses on day two.
title: The Penguins

lines.text: One day a cop pulls a van over, and when he walks up to the window he sees ten penguins in the back.
Are those your penguins?
Yes, they are my pets.
You need to take them to the zoo right now.
So the man agrees and drives off.
The next day the cop pulls over the same van, walks up to the window and sees the ten penguins all wearing sunglasses.
I thought I told you to take those penguins to the zoo.
I did, today we are going to the beach!

notes: Translated line by line, title line dropped. Two stops on the same road with a wipe for the next day; the penguin puppet stands for the ten penguins and wears dark glasses on day two.
title: Пингвины

lines.text: Однажды полицейский останавливает фургон, подходит к окну и видит, что сзади сидят десять пингвинов.
Это ваши пингвины?
Да, это мои питомцы.
Вам нужно немедленно отвезти их в зоопарк.
Мужчина соглашается и уезжает.
На следующий день полицейский останавливает тот же фургон, подходит к окну и видит десять пингвинов, и все в солнечных очках.
Я же сказал вам отвезти этих пингвинов в зоопарк.
Я и отвёз! А сегодня мы едем на пляж!

notes: Translated line by line, title line dropped. Two stops on the same road with a wipe for the next day; the penguin puppet stands for the ten penguins and wears dark glasses on day two.
title: Die Pinguine

lines.text: Eines Tages hält ein Polizist einen Lieferwagen an, und als er ans Fenster tritt, sieht er hinten zehn Pinguine sitzen.
Sind das Ihre Pinguine?
Ja, das sind meine Haustiere.
Sie müssen sie sofort in den Zoo bringen.
Der Mann ist einverstanden und fährt los.
Am nächsten Tag hält der Polizist denselben Lieferwagen an, tritt ans Fenster und sieht die zehn Pinguine, alle mit Sonnenbrillen.
Ich dachte, ich hätte Ihnen gesagt, Sie sollen die Pinguine in den Zoo bringen.
Hab ich! Heute fahren wir an den Strand!

notes: The first-person setup is spoken by the boyfriend as he walks in with the dog; 'she was livid' is shown by her face. Until a dead-dog pose exists the dog wears a halo so the viewer can tell it is dead.

lines.text: My girlfriend's dog died, so to cheer her up I got her an identical one.
What am I going to do with two dead dogs?

notes: Translated literally; the dog is the male dog puppet, so «собака» became «пёс» (rule 8). The boyfriend says the setup as he walks in; the dog wears a halo until a dead-dog pose exists.

И что мне теперь делать с двумя дохлыми псами?

Was soll ich denn jetzt mit zwei toten Hunden?

Racecar.
Ten years later.
Where's the palindrome?

notes: Source wording kept; the leader's last speech split into three lines. Scouts in khaki with badges, the leader in a campaign-style hat; the boy picks up the new snake prop after the answer; the horrified other kids are a pupils crowd.
title: Venomous

lines.text: Sir, is this snake poisonous?
No, that snake's not poisonous at all.
So the boy picks up the snake, which bites him, and the boy starts to spasm and foam at the mouth as the other kids look on in horror.
But that snake is venomous.
Poison is ingested or absorbed, while venom is injected.
Let's get it right next time, boys.

notes: Russian «ядовитая» covers both meanings, so the leader pedantically switches to the real but rare word «ядоносная» (a snake that injects venom) against «ядовитая»; the rest is translated line by line. Same staging as the original: khaki scouts, snake prop, pupils crowd.
title: Ядоносная

lines.text: Скажите, эта змея ядовитая?
Нет, эта змея совсем не ядовитая.
Мальчик берёт змею в руки, она его кусает, у мальчика начинаются судороги и пена изо рта, а остальные дети в ужасе смотрят.
Но эта змея ядоносная.
Ядовитое отравляет, если его съесть или потрогать, а ядоносное само впрыскивает яд.
В следующий раз давайте точнее, ребята.

notes: German 'giftig' covers both, so the leader pedantically uses the zoological term 'venomös' (actively venomous) against 'giftig'; the rest translated line by line. Same staging as the original: khaki scouts, snake prop, pupils crowd.
title: Venomös

lines.text: Herr Gruppenleiter, ist die Schlange giftig?
Nein, die Schlange ist überhaupt nicht giftig.
Der Junge hebt die Schlange auf, sie beißt ihn, und er bekommt Krämpfe und Schaum vor dem Mund, während die anderen Kinder entsetzt zusehen.
Aber die Schlange ist venomös.
Giftig ist, was man schluckt oder berührt, venomös ist, was injiziert wird.
Nächstes Mal machen wir es richtig, Jungs.

notes: Title line dropped, source wording kept; the husband's shout split in two. He walks into a full bar (people crowd) with the new pistol prop; the voice from the other end is a relaxed patron with a glass at the far stool.
title: More Ammo

lines.text: A guy walks into a crowded local bar, holding a pistol in his hand and yelling:
I have a forty-five caliber pistol here with seven rounds in the barrel plus one in the chamber,
and I want to know who's been sleeping with my wife!
You'll need more ammo.

notes: Line-by-line translation; caliber and rounds kept, the punch is «больше патронов». Full bar as a people crowd, pistol prop, the patron at the far stool with a glass.
title: Больше патронов

lines.text: Мужик заходит в переполненный местный бар с пистолетом в руке и кричит:
У меня тут пистолет сорок пятого калибра, семь патронов в стволе плюс один в патроннике,
и я хочу знать, кто спал с моей женой!
Тебе понадобится больше патронов.

notes: Line-by-line translation; the local bar becomes a full Kneipe (people crowd), punch is 'mehr Munition'. Pistol prop, the patron at the far stool with a glass.
title: Mehr Munition

lines.text: Ein Typ kommt mit einer Pistole in der Hand in eine volle Kneipe und brüllt:
Ich habe hier eine Pistole Kaliber fünfundvierzig mit sieben Schuss im Lauf plus einem in der Kammer,
und ich will wissen, wer mit meiner Frau geschlafen hat!
Da brauchst du mehr Munition.

notes: Monologue kept word for word, split in three. The neighbour stands silently at the door; the man picks up the new bagpipes prop right before the punchline so the reveal lands on it.
title: Two Thirty

lines.text: My neighbour knocked on my door at two thirty this morning.
Can you believe that, two thirty?!
Luckily for him I was still up playing my bagpipes.
